children: The US dollar started the week by stepping back from its highest level in more than a year and a half. In early Asian trade on Monday, November 23, the greenback eased as investors regained some composure following last week's selloff.

The trigger was a recalibration of Federal Reserve expectations. Traders trimmed their bets that the central bank will hike interest rates aggressively at its meeting next month, and the dollar gave back a little of its recent swagger.
The US dollar index, or DXY, opened lower at 103.80. That follows a recent peak near 103.9, the strongest reading in 19 months.
Other currencies took the opening. The euro climbed 0.1% to $1.0974, while the Australian dollar gained 0.2% to $0.6629.

Futures markets still lean heavily toward tighter policy. Pricing points to an 88.6% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting, with just an 11.4% chance that rates stay put.

The dollar's climb to its 19-month peak was built on solid US economic data. October consumer price index figures, released on November 10, showed inflation running strong enough to put rate hikes firmly back on the table.
Fed officials then leaned into that message. Hawkish commentary, particularly from Governor Christopher Waller, reinforced the idea that the central bank was prepared to tighten further.
Robust job growth figures added fuel. Put together, the inflation print, the jobs data and the tough talk from Fed officials created a near-perfect setup for a dollar rally.

The broader view on the dollar remains constructive. Eric Robertsen of Standard Chartered expects the greenback to outperform, citing favorable interest rate differentials and the relative strength of the US economy.
Analysts also point to productivity gains and a perception of lower political risk in the US compared with other economies.

The next few weeks offer several clear checkpoints. Incoming US inflation and employment data will shape whether the 88.6% hike probability firms up or fades. Any further comments from Fed officials, especially Waller and his colleagues, will be parsed closely for hints about the pace of tightening beyond December.
Either way, the December 8-9 meeting now looms as the main event.

title: Dollar eases from 19-month high as market confidence recovers
